model.name: Facility
model.purpose: Governed context model for a Facility as an operational aggregate in the built environment: a collection of assets constructed, installed or established to serve an entity's needs, located as a distinct real-property object, and used as a spatial container that may hold buildings, other facility types and facility parts.
model.scope_statement: This model covers the identity, classification, location, composition, ownership, authority, lifecycle, operations, regulatory interest, safety, information governance and interoperability of a Facility as a format-neutral world-model aggregate. A Facility is not land (Site), not a single shelter structure (Building), not a single equipment asset, and not the facility-management function or management system that operates it. The model is independent of JSON, YAML, BIM files, GIS layers, registries, MCP or document stores; those are projections of the same semantics.
in_scope: Identity of a facility as a distinct operational and real-property object, including master-system identifiers, governed IRIs and Dimension-assigned UUIDs or ULIDs.
Classification of facility type, function, industrial activity and occupancy or use sufficient to operate and regulate the facility.
Spatial location, georeferencing, postal and jurisdictional placement, and composition relative to a containing Site and contained Buildings, structures or facility parts.
Owner, operator, demand organization, facility-management organization, affiliations, tenure and authority-having-jurisdiction relationships.
Lifecycle from establishment through commissioning, in-service operation, trigger events, change of occupancy, transfer, mothballing, decommissioning and demolition.
Facility services, service levels, occupant load, hours of operation, systems that service the facility, and operational performance evidence.
Regulatory program interests, permits and linked program-system identifiers where a facility is an object of environmental or safety regulation.
Asset information model, common data environment, provenance, matching quality, access, retention and alignment to external schemas.
out_of_scope: Site as a defined area of land or cadastral parcel, including land-title geometry as the primary object; that belongs to WM-BLT-008 Site.
Building or structure as a shelter object, storeys, spaces, rooms, workstations and interior elements; those belong to WM-BLT-001 Building and finer spatial models.
A single equipment item, vehicle, furniture item or air-handling unit treated as the facility itself.

The facility-management organizational function, management system, SLA commercial terms and sourcing strategy as first-class objects (ISO 41001/41011 FM), except where they must be referenced to operate the facility.
Infrastructure as a system of facilities, equipment and services; that is a sibling aggregate above this model.
Real-estate legal estate, cadastre and undeveloped land as property-law objects, except tenure and address needed to locate and authorize the facility.
Organization, person, contract and financial ledgers as master objects.
Nature preserves and other unbuilt assets that have not been constructed, installed or established to serve an entity's needs.
Incident, inspection, work-order and sensor time-series streams, except as trigger events that update facility state or the asset information model.

boundary_notes.distinction: A Site is a defined area of land, possibly covered with water, on which construction or operation occurs. A Facility is the operational collection of assets established on one or more sites to serve an entity's needs. EPA Facility Registry Service often treats facility and site as a combined facility-site record; this model keeps them distinct and records that conflation as an alignment conflict.

A Building is construction work that provides shelter and is designed to stand permanently in one place. A Facility may contain one or more buildings or structures, and may also be a non-building facility such as a road, railway, bridge or marine facility. IFC 4.3 models IfcBuilding as a subtype of IfcFacility; this Vercy model does not adopt that subtype relationship and instead uses CONTAINS. That conflict is an alignment, not a claim of IFC conformance.

An asset is an item, thing or entity of potential or actual value. A facility is a collection of such assets constructed, installed or established to serve needs. ISO 19650-3 uses asset as a convenience term covering both asset management and facility management; this model keeps the facility as the operational aggregate and references assets rather than absorbing the asset register.
Infrastructure is a system of facilities, equipment and services needed for the operation of an organization. Individual facilities are members of that system; the system itself is out of scope here.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Real estate and legal parcel models
boundary_notes.distinction: Real estate is immoveable property including structures, grounds and undeveloped land. Facility uses tenure, address and land-title references to locate and authorize occupation, but does not own cadastral legal semantics.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Organization, demand organization and FM organization
boundary_notes.distinction: A facility is a place-and-asset aggregate. The demand organization is the entity whose needs the facility serves; the FM organization delivers facility services. FHIR Location.managingOrganization is an alignment for operator, not a substitute for the physical facility.

FHIR Location covers incidental and dedicated places from freezers and beds to hospital buildings and mobile clinics. This model is the operational facility aggregate, not every service location, bed, vehicle or kind-of-location classifier.

ISO 41011 defines facility as the asset collection and facility management as the organizational function that integrates people, place and process. The management system, policy, strategy and SLA are referenced from this model; they are not the Facility object.

sources.title: ISO 41011:2024 Facility management — Vocabulary
sources.relevance: Normative definition of facility as a collection of assets constructed, installed or established to serve an entity's needs; also demand organization, FM organization, facility service, facility life cycle, service life, facility plan, post-occupancy evaluation, end-of-life and related FM vocabulary.

sources.title: ISO 6707-4:2021 Buildings and civil engineering works — Vocabulary — Part 4: Facility management terms
sources.relevance: Construction-industry vocabulary for facility, facility-in-service, real estate, infrastructure, workplace, security zone and related FM terms complementary to ISO 41011.

sources.title: Facility Site Identification Data Standard, Standard No. EX000020.2
sources.organization: United States Environmental Protection Agency / Exchange Network Leadership Council
sources.relevance: US environmental master-data standard defining a facility as a distinct real-property entity, unique facility-site identifier, name, type, federal-facility indicator, location address, coordinates, affiliations, SIC/NAICS and environmental interest.

sources.title: FRS Description (Facility Registry Service)
sources.relevance: Authoritative description of the US Facility Registry Service, Registry ID format, program-system linkage, matching, best-pick coordinates and data-steward roles.

sources.title: IfcFacility — IFC 4.3.2.0 Documentation
sources.relevance: Open BIM spatial-structure entity for a facility that may be a building, bridge, railway, road or marine facility; composition, placement, containment, GlobalId, OwnerHistory and occupancy, agreement, risk and fire-safety property sets.

sources.title: ISO 19650-3:2020 Organization and digitization of information about buildings and civil engineering works, including building information modelling (BIM) — Information management using building information modelling — Part 3: Operational phase of the assets
sources.relevance: Operational-phase information management, asset information model, trigger events, PIM-to-AIM handover, transfer of information on ownership change, and the relationship of facility management to asset management.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR Release 4 — Resource Location
sources.relevance: Healthcare and service-location identity, status, type, address, WGS84 position, managing organization, part-of hierarchy, hours of operation and the distinction between physical Location and Organization.
