sources.relevance: Scope of FM and explicit exclusion that a single asset is not a facility and that something not built, such as a nature preserve, is not a facility even if it is an asset.

sources.title: 2021 International Building Code (IBC) — Section 111.1 Change of occupancy
sources.relevance: Model building-code rule that a building or structure shall not be used or occupied, and that a change of occupancy shall not be made, until the building official has issued a certificate of occupancy.

sources.title: IfcSite — IFC 4.3.2.0 Documentation
sources.relevance: Site as defined land area and optional parent of IfcFacility; WGS84 latitude, longitude and elevation; land title number; postal address; and the spatial hierarchy against which Facility is placed.

sources.title: Detailed Facility Report Data Dictionary
sources.relevance: Operating data elements for a regulated facility: FRS ID, name, address, coordinates and datum, NAICS/SIC, Indian country, program identifiers, compliance status and inactive-facility indication.

sources.title: Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) — buildingSMART International
sources.relevance: States that IFC 4.3.2.0 is the latest official IFC and is published by ISO as ISO 16739-1:2024 for data sharing in construction and facility management, including infrastructure facilities.

bundles.name: Identity and classification
bundles.description: How a facility is uniquely identified, named and typed as an operational and real-property object, including master-system identifiers, aliases, facility type, industrial classification and occupancy or use.
bundles.rationale: Agents cannot create, match or operate a facility without a governed identity and a classification that supports both operational use and regulatory interest. Primary sources disagree on whether identity is a registry ID, an IFC GlobalId or a healthcare location identifier; the model must record all three as alignments under a single identity-priority rule.

layers.name: Identifiers and names
layers.description: Master-system identifiers, governed IRIs, Dimension-assigned UUIDs or ULIDs, public names and aliases.

findings.name: Authoritative facility identifiers
findings.description: A facility must carry at least one identifier, with priority: the identifier assigned by the authoritative master system in the operating jurisdiction or domain; a governed global identifier or IRI; then a UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. Dates are not identifiers. EPA FRS assigns a Registry ID such as 110012345678; IFC assigns IfcRoot.GlobalId; FHIR Location.identifier is a business identifier. Program-system IDs (permit IDs, TRI IDs) are linked alternate identifiers, not the master facility key.

questions.text: What is the authoritative master-system identifier for this facility, which system issued it, and in what identifier context?
What governed IRI, IFC GlobalId, FHIR identifier or Dimension UUID or ULID is assigned, and which of these is canonical inside this Dimension?
Which program-system or permit identifiers are linked to this facility and must not be treated as the master facility key?
Has this identifier been merged, split or superseded, and what surviving master identifier should agents use?

data_elements.name: Master facility identifier
data_elements.description: Unique identification number used by the authoritative master system to identify the facility site or facility.

data_elements.name: Identifier context
data_elements.description: Source or data system that created or defined the identifier.

data_elements.name: IFC globally unique identifier
data_elements.description: IfcRoot.GlobalId for the facility occurrence in an IFC exchange, unique within the software world of that exchange.

data_elements.name: Dimension UUID or ULID
data_elements.description: UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master-system identifier yet exists.

data_elements.name: Linked program identifiers
data_elements.description: Cross-references to program records such as permit IDs that reside in other systems.

artifacts.name: Facility identity record
artifacts.description: Governed identity record holding master, alternate and Dimension identifiers with issuer context.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system identifier first; then governed IRI; then Dimension UUID or ULID. Never use a date as an identifier.

findings.name: Facility names and aliases
findings.description: The public or commercial name of a facility as it appears on invoices, signs or business documents, plus long names and historical aliases. EPA notes that names may differ across databases after ownership change or use of parent versus site name. FHIR Location.alias records past names. IFC provides Name and LongName.

questions.text: What is the current public or commercial name of the facility as used on signs, invoices or the master registry?
What aliases, former names or long names are known, including names used after ownership change?
Which name is canonical for matching and public display, and which names are known to be ambiguous or parent-organization names?

data_elements.name: Facility site name
data_elements.description: Public or commercial name of the facility site.

data_elements.name: Long name
data_elements.description: Informal long name used with the short Name in IFC spatial structure.

data_elements.name: Aliases and former names
data_elements.description: Alternate or historical names by which the location or facility is known.

artifacts.name: Naming and alias record
artifacts.description: Record of canonical name, aliases and the source of each name.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Name is not an identifier; link names to the master facility identifier.

layers.name: Typology and use
layers.description: Facility type, function, industrial classification and occupancy or use classification.

findings.name: Facility type and function
findings.description: ISO 41011 defines a facility by the needs it serves. EPA FacilitySiteTypeCode represents the type of site a facility occupies. IFC IfcFacility may be instantiated as IfcBuilding, IfcBridge, IfcRailway, IfcRoad, IfcMarineFacility or a user-defined ObjectType when no subtype exists. FHIR Location.type is the function performed; Location.physicalType is the physical form. These code systems are alignments, not a single universal taxonomy.

questions.text: What facility type or physical form is asserted, in which classification scheme, and is it a building, civil facility, mixed complex or other?
What operational function or service-delivery role does the facility perform for the demand organization?
Should a more specific IFC or local subtype be used instead of generic facility, and what agreed ObjectType is used if not?
Do EPA type, IFC subtype and FHIR type or physicalType conflict for this facility, and which type is used for which process?

data_elements.name: Facility site type code
data_elements.description: Designator for the type of site a facility occupies, with code-list metadata.

data_elements.name: IFC facility entity or object type
data_elements.description: IfcFacility or a subtype, or IfcFacility.ObjectType when a dedicated subtype is unavailable.

data_elements.name: Function or service type
data_elements.description: Type of function performed at the location.

data_elements.name: Physical form
data_elements.description: Physical form of the location, for example building versus vehicle.

artifacts.name: Facility type assignment
artifacts.description: Typed classification assignment with scheme, version and any user-defined type agreement.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify the assignment by facility master identifier plus classification scheme and version.

findings.name: Industrial and occupancy classification
findings.description: A facility may carry NAICS and SIC industrial classifications for environmental and statistical reporting, and an occupancy or use classification that governs legal occupation of buildings or structures. IBC Section 111 forbids use, occupancy or change of occupancy without a certificate of occupancy. Occupancy group enumerations live in IBC Chapter 3 and equivalent national codes; they are jurisdictional alignments, not a global facility taxonomy. IFC Pset_SpaceOccupancyRequirements on IfcFacility records occupancy type and numbers.

questions.text: What NAICS or SIC codes classify the industrial activity of this facility, which is primary, and from which program system were they taken?
What occupancy or use classification and division apply under the adopted building code, and to which portion of the facility?
Is the facility mixed occupancy or mixed use, and how are portions classified and authorized separately?
Which edition of the building or occupancy code was in force when the current occupancy was authorized?

data_elements.name: NAICS codes
data_elements.description: Six-digit North American Industry Classification System codes for the facility.

data_elements.name: SIC codes
data_elements.description: Standard Industrial Classification codes for the facility.

data_elements.name: Occupancy or use classification
data_elements.description: Use and occupancy classification under the adopted building code for the facility or a described portion.

data_elements.name: Governing code edition
data_elements.description: Edition of the code under which occupancy was authorized.

artifacts.name: Classification and occupancy evidence
artifacts.description: Industrial classification assignments and occupancy classification statements tied to the adopted code edition.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Certificate or classification record number issued by the AHJ or classifying agency; fall back to facility master identifier plus scheme and version.

bundles.name: Spatial composition and location
bundles.description: Where the facility is, how it is georeferenced, and how it composes with Site, Buildings, facility parts and non-building facility types.
bundles.rationale: Facility is both a real-property location and a spatial container. IFC places IfcFacility under IfcProject or IfcSite and allows facility complexes and parts. EPA locates a facility by address and coordinates. The known Vercy relation is Site CONTAINS Facility CONTAINS Building; IFC instead subtypes Building under Facility.

layers.name: Location and georeference
layers.description: Postal and physical address, geopolitical descriptors and geographic coordinates with datum, method and accuracy.

findings.name: Physical address and jurisdiction
findings.description: EPA requires a location address for the front door or main entrance, including street, locality, state, postal code, country, county and tribe. IFC SiteAddress and land title number sit on IfcSite; FHIR Location.address is the physical location. Jurisdictional fields include EPA region and Indian-country status. Mailing address is affiliation data, not the facility location.

questions.text: What is the physical location address of the main entrance or front door, including locality, region, postal code and country?
Which administrative, tribal, regional or building-code jurisdictions apply to this facility?
Is this address the containing site, the facility entrance, a mailing address, or a parent-organization address, and how was that distinguished?
What land-title, cadastral or parcel references locate the facility without making this model the legal parcel register?

data_elements.name: Facility location address
data_elements.description: Physical geographic address of the front door or main entrance.

data_elements.name: Indian country indicator
data_elements.description: Whether the facility is in Indian country as defined for US environmental programs.

data_elements.name: Land title number
data_elements.description: Land title designation associated with the site that contains the facility.

data_elements.name: Authority-having-jurisdiction
data_elements.description: Building official or other AHJ whose occupancy and permit rules apply.

artifacts.name: Standardized location address record
artifacts.description: Parsed and standardized location address with jurisdictional descriptors.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bind address to the facility master identifier; do not use address text as an identifier.

findings.name: Coordinates and georeferencing
findings.description: A facility is located by latitude and longitude, usually front-door or centroid, with method, accuracy, geometric type, datum and reference point. EPA FRS applies a weekly best-pick process. ECHO reports NAD83. IFC recommends project-level IfcCoordinateReferenceSystem for precise georeferencing and allows approximate WGS84 on IfcSite. FHIR Location.position uses WGS84. Multiple coordinates may exist; each coordinate instance locates one facility.

questions.text: What are the authoritative latitude, longitude and optional elevation or altitude, and in which geodetic datum?
What collection method, geometric type, reference point and horizontal accuracy apply to the coordinate, and is it a best-pick or ZIP centroid approximation?
When was the coordinate observed or surveyed, and when was it ingested or last refreshed in the registry?
Is facility placement absolute in a world CRS, relative to a site, or relative to a facility complex, and which CRS or map conversion is used?

data_elements.name: Latitude measure
data_elements.description: Latitude of the facility reference point.

data_elements.name: Longitude measure
data_elements.description: Longitude of the facility reference point.

data_elements.name: Coordinate method and accuracy
data_elements.description: Datum, collection method, geometric type, reference point and accuracy.

data_elements.name: Facility geometry
data_elements.description: Optional footprint, boundary or representative point geometry for the facility.

artifacts.name: Facility geolocation record
artifacts.description: Coordinate set with datum, method, accuracy, best-pick status and observation versus ingestion times.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by facility master identifier plus coordinate role and observation time; never treat a timestamp as the facility identifier.

layers.name: Composition and spatial structure
layers.description: Containment by Site, containment of Buildings and facility parts, composition type, and non-building or mobile facilities.

findings.name: Site, building and part composition
findings.description: IFC spatial composition is a hierarchical tree: IfcProject, IfcSite, IfcFacility or subtype, IfcFacilityPart or IfcBuildingStorey, and IfcSpace. A facility may be assigned directly to a project with no site, to a site, or to another facility as a section. Vercy known relations: Site CONTAINS Facility CONTAINS Building. IFC also allows IfcBuilding as a subtype of IfcFacility; this model records that as a conflict and does not claim IFC conformance. A facility may exist without a site. Whether one operational facility may span multiple sites is unresolved.

questions.text: Which Site contains this facility, or is the facility the outermost spatial container with no site recorded?
Which buildings, structures or facility parts does this facility contain, and is the relation spatial containment or operational aggregation?
Is this facility a complex, an element or a part, and if it nests under another facility what are the composition-type constraints?
Does the operational facility span multiple sites, share a site with other facilities, or interfere spatially with another facility?

data_elements.name: Containing site
data_elements.description: Reference to the Site spatial container, if any.

data_elements.name: Contained buildings or structures
data_elements.description: Buildings or structures aggregated into the operational facility.

data_elements.name: Composition type
data_elements.description: COMPLEX, ELEMENT or PARTIAL composition of the spatial structure element; default ELEMENT.

data_elements.name: Parent facility
data_elements.description: Another facility that is the spatial container, for example a complex or a section parent.

data_elements.name: Part-of location
data_elements.description: FHIR-style physical part-of relationship to another location.

artifacts.name: Spatial structure composition graph
artifacts.description: Typed containment and aggregation edges among Project, Site, Facility, FacilityPart and Building.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Edge identity is the pair of endpoint master identifiers plus relation type; node identity follows facility or sibling-model identity priority.

findings.name: Non-building, mobile and exclusion cases
findings.description: ISO 16739-1:2024 / IFC 4.3 extends facility to bridges, roads, railways, waterways and port facilities. FHIR includes mobile clinics, ambulances and vehicles. EPA includes monitoring stations and waste sites that cannot be classified as single facilities. ISO/TR 41013 states that a single asset such as a car or air-handling unit is not a facility, and that something not built, such as a nature preserve, is not a facility. Mobile versus fixed and instance versus kind must be explicit. Kind-of-location classifiers are out of scope as instances.

questions.text: Is this a building-oriented facility, a civil or infrastructure facility, or a mixed campus, and which IFC or local subtype applies?
Is the facility fixed, mobile or relocatable, and if mobile what is the current position versus the home base?
Does the candidate fail the facility test because it is a single asset, an unbuilt asset, a kind classifier, or a space or room?

data_elements.name: Mobility mode
data_elements.description: Fixed, mobile or relocatable operating mode.

data_elements.name: Instance or kind
data_elements.description: Whether the record is a specific instance or a kind-of-facility classifier; kind is out of scope for this aggregate.

data_elements.name: Not-a-facility flag
data_elements.description: Explicit exclusion when the candidate is a single asset or unbuilt asset.

artifacts.name: Facility eligibility decision
artifacts.description: Decision record that a candidate is or is not a facility under ISO 41011/41013 and this model.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Decision identifier assigned by the Dimension; cite the candidate's source identifier.

bundles.name: Parties, ownership and authority
bundles.description: Who owns, operates, demands, occupies and authorizes the facility, including federal-facility status, affiliations and occupancy certificates.
bundles.rationale: ISO 41011 separates demand organization, FM organization, service provider and user. EPA models affiliations of organizations and persons to a facility site and a federal-facility indicator. FHIR Location.managingOrganization is the organization responsible for provisioning and upkeep. IBC makes the building official the occupancy authority. IFC Pset_PropertyAgreement captures lease or property agreement terms.

layers.name: Ownership and operation
layers.description: Owner, operator, demand organization, FM organization, federal status and contacts.

findings.name: Owner, operator and demand organization
findings.description: The demand organization has the need and authority to incur cost. The FM organization is responsible for facility management and may be internal or outsourced. EPA distinguishes facilities owned or operated by the Federal Government. Owner, operator and occupier may differ, and names in FRS may reflect parent rather than site operator. Continuity of the asset information model is required when ownership transfers.

questions.text: Who is the legal owner of the facility or of the land it occupies, and is ownership federal, public, private or mixed?
Which party is the demand organization, which is the FM organization or operator, and is service delivery in-house, outsourced or co-sourced?
What is the effective interval of each owner, operator or demand-organization role, and what happens to the AIM on transfer?

data_elements.name: Owner party
data_elements.description: Party that owns the facility or the land it occupies.

data_elements.name: Demand organization
data_elements.description: Entity that has the need and authority to incur costs to have requirements met.

data_elements.name: Facility management organization
data_elements.description: Organization responsible for facility management.

data_elements.name: Federal facility indicator
data_elements.description: Whether the facility is owned or operated by a federal governmental unit.

artifacts.name: Facility party-role assignment
artifacts.description: Time-bounded assignment of owner, operator, demand organization and FM organization.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Assignment identifier plus facility master identifier and party identifier; time interval is not an identifier.

findings.name: Affiliations, contacts and tenure
findings.description: EPA Facility Site Affiliation is the relationship between a facility site and an organization or person, optionally with a mailing address. IFC Pset_PropertyAgreement records agreement type, tracking identifier, commencement and termination dates, duration, options, restrictions and condition at commencement and termination. Due diligence under ISO 41011 is the appraisal of facility information for physical, functional, financial and environmental performance.

questions.text: Which organizations and persons are affiliated with the facility, in what role, and what are their contacts and mailing addresses?
Is the facility owned, leased or otherwise occupied, and what are the agreement type, identifier, commencement, termination, options and restrictions?
Has due diligence been completed for a sale, lease or appointment, and what gaps remain in physical, functional, financial or environmental evidence?

data_elements.name: Facility affiliations
data_elements.description: Relationships between the facility and organizations or persons.

data_elements.name: Property agreement
data_elements.description: Lease or property agreement terms attached to the facility.

data_elements.name: Due diligence status
data_elements.description: Status of compilation and validation of facility information for transfer or appointment.

artifacts.name: Property or occupancy agreement
artifacts.description: Lease, licence or property agreement governing tenure of the facility.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Agreement tracking identifier assigned by the issuing party; bind to facility master identifier.

layers.name: Occupancy authority
layers.description: Certificate of occupancy, change of occupancy and the building official as authority.

findings.name: Occupancy authorization and authority having jurisdiction
findings.description: Under IBC 111.1, a building or structure shall not be used or occupied, and a change of occupancy shall not be made, until the building official has issued a certificate of occupancy. Certificates that presume authority to violate the code are not valid. Work exempt from permit may be excepted. This rule is building-code-centric; roads, railways and some civil facilities are authorized by other AHJs. A CO authorizes occupancy under the building code; it does not by itself satisfy ongoing fire-code, elevator or environmental program duties. Phased projects may require occupancy authorization before occupying portions.

questions.text: Has a certificate of occupancy or equivalent occupancy authorization been issued for this facility or a described portion, and by which AHJ?
What use, occupancy classification, construction type, code edition and design occupant load does the certificate authorize?
Is occupancy authorized in phases or for only a portion of the facility, and what is still prohibited?
When was the certificate issued or occupancy authorized, and when was that fact observed or ingested into this model?

data_elements.name: Occupancy authorization status
data_elements.description: Whether legal occupancy is authorized, prohibited, partial or not applicable because the facility is not a building or structure under the adopted code.

data_elements.name: Certificate of occupancy identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the building official to the certificate.

data_elements.name: Design occupant load
data_elements.description: Design occupant load stated for the authorized occupancy.

data_elements.name: Building official or AHJ
data_elements.description: Authority that inspects and issues occupancy authorization.

artifacts.name: Certificate of occupancy
artifacts.description: Occupancy authorization issued by the building official for a building, structure or described portion.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Certificate number issued by the AHJ; bind to facility master identifier and portion.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, state and events
bundles.description: Operational status, facility-in-service, work stages, trigger events, change of occupancy, transfer, mothballing, decommissioning and demolition.
bundles.rationale: ISO 41011 defines facility life cycle as consecutive interlinked stages and includes post-occupancy evaluation, mobilization, demobilization and end-of-life costs for decommissioning, deconstruction and demolition. ISO 6707-4 defines facility-in-service. ISO 19650-3 defines scheduled and unscheduled trigger events and PIM-to-AIM handover. IBC 111 governs change of occupancy. FHIR Location.status is active, suspended or inactive.

layers.name: Status and in-service condition
layers.description: Whether the facility is established, commissioned, occupied, suspended, inactive or in-service.

findings.name: Operational status and facility-in-service
findings.description: Facility-in-service is the facility as completed, commissioned, handed over and in operation mode. FHIR status values are active, suspended and inactive. ECHO maps inactive facility or system as a distinct cartographic state. Status is not identity. Commissioning and closeout, including PIM-to-AIM transfer at the start of the operational phase, are distinct from legal occupancy authorization.

questions.text: What is the current operational status of the facility, and is it in-service, suspended, inactive, mothballed or not yet commissioned?
Has commissioning, handover and transfer from the project information model to the asset information model been completed?
Do registry, BIM, healthcare-location and environmental-program statuses agree, and which status is used for which operating process?

data_elements.name: Operational status
data_elements.description: Current operating state such as active, suspended, inactive, mothballed or decommissioned.

data_elements.name: Facility-in-service flag
data_elements.description: Whether the facility is completed, commissioned, handed over and in operation mode.

data_elements.name: PIM to AIM transfer status
data_elements.description: Status of information transfer from the delivery-phase project information model to the operational asset information model.

artifacts.name: Commissioning and handover record
artifacts.description: Evidence that the facility was commissioned and that relevant PIM information was transferred into the AIM.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Handover or commissioning record identifier assigned by the appointing party; bind to facility master identifier.

layers.name: Events, change of occupancy and end of life
layers.description: Trigger events during operation, change of occupancy, transfer, mothballing, decommissioning and demolition.

findings.name: Operational trigger events
findings.description: ISO 19650-3 applies both to trigger events that are scheduled in advance, such as annual maintenance, estate reviews and call-off repairs, and to unscheduled or unforeseeable events such as breakdowns, accidents and extreme floods. Acquisition from an existing owner is a distinct information-exchange event. Post-occupancy evaluation is a defined process after users have occupied the facility. Event time and observation or ingestion time must be recorded separately.

questions.text: What trigger event occurred or is scheduled, of what type, and is it planned, unplanned or an ownership acquisition?
What AIM, status, occupancy or composition updates does this trigger event require, and which appointed party will produce them?
What is the event time, and what is the observation or ingestion time of the record?

data_elements.name: Trigger event type
data_elements.description: Class of operational trigger, including scheduled maintenance, breakdown, accident, flood, renovation, evaluation or acquisition.

data_elements.name: Event time
data_elements.description: When the trigger event occurred or is scheduled, in RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Observation or ingestion time
data_elements.description: When the event was observed or ingested into the governed store.

artifacts.name: Trigger event record
artifacts.description: Governed record of an operational trigger and the AIM update it requires.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Event record identifier assigned by the Dimension or appointing party; not the event date.

findings.name: Change of occupancy, mothballing and end of life
findings.description: Change of occupancy of a building or structure requires a new certificate of occupancy. ISO 41011 includes facility life cycle stages, demobilization of facility services, and end-of-life costs for decommissioning, deconstruction, demolition, recycling and making environmentally safe. Rare but in-scope states include mothballing (inactive but not demolished), adaptive reuse, partial demolition, and continued environmental interest after operations cease. Environmental decommissioning of regulated materials is a US EPA program concern and must be linked rather than duplicated.

questions.text: Is a change of occupancy or use proposed or complete, and has the AHJ issued a new occupancy authorization?
Is the facility being renovated, adaptively reused, mothballed, decommissioned, deconstructed or demolished, and what regulated-material constraints apply?
Have facility services been demobilized, and do environmental or safety program interests remain after operations cease?

data_elements.name: Facility life-cycle stage
data_elements.description: Current consecutive stage of the facility over time.

data_elements.name: End-of-life path
data_elements.description: Chosen path among renovation, adaptive reuse, mothball, decommission, deconstruct or demolish.

data_elements.name: Demobilization status
data_elements.description: Status of transferring facility services back to the demand organization or a new provider, or of ending services.

artifacts.name: End-of-life or change-of-occupancy decision
artifacts.description: Decision and authorization package for change of occupancy, mothballing, decommissioning or demolition.
artifacts.identity_strategy: AHJ or owner decision identifier; bind to facility master identifier.

bundles.name: Operations, services and performance
bundles.description: Facility services, service levels, hours of operation, occupant load, systems serving the facility, and performance measurement including post-occupancy evaluation.
bundles.rationale: A facility exists to serve needs. ISO 41011 defines facility service, service level agreement, workplace and post-occupancy evaluation. IFC records occupancy requirements and systems that service spatial elements. FHIR records hours of operation and availability exceptions.

layers.name: Services and systems
layers.description: Facility services delivered at the facility and systems that service it.

findings.name: Facility services and service levels
findings.description: A facility service is a support provision to the primary activities of an organization, delivered by an internal or external provider. Service level is the complete description of requirements; an SLA is the agreed document on performance, measurement and conditions. ISO/TR 41013 notes that FM integrates a broad scope of processes enabling cost-effective, safe workplaces, and that isolated non-integrated service lines do not by themselves constitute FM. This model records which services are delivered at the facility; it does not own the commercial SLA object.

questions.text: Which facility services are delivered at this facility, by which provider, and are they in-house, outsourced or co-sourced?
What service-level requirements and measurement conditions apply at this facility, and where is the SLA referenced?
Are services mobilized, in steady operation, or being demobilized, and what resources and data were established at start-up?

data_elements.name: Facility services
data_elements.description: Support services delivered at the facility.

data_elements.name: Service level references
data_elements.description: References to agreed service-level documents.

data_elements.name: Mobilization status
data_elements.description: Whether resources, systems, data and procedures have been established for service delivery.

artifacts.name: Facility service-delivery map
artifacts.description: Map of services, providers and service-level references for the facility.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bind services to facility master identifier plus service type and provider.

findings.name: Systems servicing the facility
findings.description: IFC IfcRelServicesBuildings relates systems that provide a service to the spatial element. Facility plan physical assets include building services and systems. Detailed system design belongs in sibling system and building models; this finding only records which systems service the facility as a whole.

questions.text: Which mechanical, electrical, fire, transport or other systems service this facility as a spatial container?
Are servicing systems contained in this facility, referenced from another spatial structure, or spanning several facilities?
What commissioning or performance evidence shows that servicing systems meet the facility's required functions?

data_elements.name: Servicing systems
data_elements.description: Systems related to the facility by a services-buildings or equivalent relation.

artifacts.name: System-to-facility service relation set
artifacts.description: Set of relations from systems to the facility they service.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Relation identity is system identifier plus facility master identifier plus relation type.

layers.name: Occupancy, hours and performance
layers.description: Occupant load, hours of operation, accessibility and post-occupancy evaluation.

findings.name: Occupant load, hours and accessibility
findings.description: IFC occupancy requirements include occupancy type, occupancy number, peak occupancy, occupancy time per day and area per occupant. FHIR records days of week, opening and closing times, all-day flags and availability exceptions. IFC Pset_SpaceCommon includes PubliclyAccessible and HandicapAccessible. ISO 41011 defines workplace as the physical location where work is performed and workspace as a zone for a work task; those finer objects are referenced, not duplicated.

questions.text: What design occupant load, typical occupancy number and peak occupancy apply, and over what occupancy time per day?
What are the usual hours of operation, including days of week and availability exceptions?
Is the facility publicly accessible, and is it designated handicap accessible at the facility aggregate level?

data_elements.name: Occupancy number
data_elements.description: Typical and peak occupancy counts and occupancy time per day.

data_elements.name: Hours of operation
data_elements.description: Usual weekly opening pattern and exceptions.

data_elements.name: Publicly accessible
data_elements.description: Whether the facility is publicly accessible.

data_elements.name: Handicap accessible
data_elements.description: Whether the facility is designated accessible to persons with disabilities at this aggregate level.

artifacts.name: Occupancy and hours record
artifacts.description: Occupant-load and operating-hours statement for the facility.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bind to facility master identifier; version by effective interval, not by date-as-ID.

findings.name: Performance evaluation and service life
findings.description: Service life is the period after installation during which a building or its parts meet performance requirements. Post-occupancy evaluation analyses how functional and comfortable a building is after users have occupied it. ISO 19650-3 includes post-occupancy or implementation evaluation as a point on the operational timeline. Key performance indicators and indoor environmental quality are measurement alignments; detailed energy-benchmarking schemes such as ENERGY STAR are known omissions unless later aligned.

questions.text: What service-life period and performance requirements apply to the facility or its major parts?
Has a post-occupancy or implementation evaluation been completed, when, and what outcomes were recorded?
Which key performance indicators are governed at facility level, including any indoor environmental quality measures, and what is the current result?

data_elements.name: Service life
data_elements.description: Period after installation during which the facility or its parts meet performance requirements.

data_elements.name: Key performance indicators
data_elements.description: Measures that provide essential information about performance at facility level.

data_elements.name: Post-occupancy evaluation status
data_elements.description: Whether and when post-occupancy evaluation has been performed.

artifacts.name: Post-occupancy evaluation report
artifacts.description: Analysis of function, comfort and performance after occupation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Report identifier assigned by the appointing or evaluating party; bind to facility master identifier.

bundles.name: Regulatory interest and compliance
bundles.description: Environmental and other program interests, permits, program-system linkages and compliance monitoring status for facilities that are regulated objects.
bundles.rationale: EPA FIDS requires that each facility site be monitored by one or more environmental interests. FRS links program records to a Registry ID. ECHO exposes statute-specific permits, inspections and compliance status. These are US-centric alignments; other jurisdictions have analogous facility registers. Ongoing program duties are distinct from a certificate of occupancy.

layers.name: Program interest and permits
layers.description: Environmental interests, statutes and permit or program identifiers linked to the facility.

findings.name: Environmental interests and program links
findings.description: An environmental interest is a permit or regulatory program associated with the facility. FRS assigns a Registry ID and then links program-system identifiers. ECHO statutes include CAA, CWA, RCRA, SDWA, EPCRA/TRI, TSCA and others. A facility may have many program records and still one master facility identity. Absence of an FRS ID does not mean a facility lacks other-jurisdiction regulatory identity.

questions.text: Which environmental or regulatory program interests apply to this facility, under which statute, and in which program system?
What permits or program authorizations are in force, expired or pending, and what are their identifiers and effective intervals?
Are all known program records linked to the same master facility identifier, or are split or duplicate facility records still open?

data_elements.name: Environmental interests
data_elements.description: Permits or regulatory programs monitoring the facility site.

data_elements.name: Program system links
data_elements.description: Linkages from program records to the master facility identifier.

artifacts.name: Program interest index
artifacts.description: Index of linked program-system records and permits for the facility.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master facility identifier plus program system acronym and program identifier.

findings.name: Compliance monitoring status
findings.description: ECHO reports compliance monitoring activity counts, last monitoring date and statute-specific compliance status, including inactive facility. These determinations often reflect alleged rather than finally adjudicated violations. This finding is an alignment to US environmental operating data; it is not a universal compliance model and must not be treated as a court judgement.

questions.text: What is the current reported compliance status by statute, and as of which refresh date?
When did the last compliance monitoring activity occur, of what type, and is the date an on-site inspection or an evaluation completion date?
Is the reported violation or noncompliance an alleged status used for tracking, or a final adjudication, and what caveats apply?

data_elements.name: Compliance status by statute
data_elements.description: Most recent reported compliance status for each regulating statute.

data_elements.name: Last compliance monitoring activity
data_elements.description: Type and time of the most recent counted monitoring activity.

artifacts.name: Compliance status snapshot
artifacts.description: Point-in-time extract of reported compliance and monitoring status.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Facility master identifier plus snapshot ingestion time.

bundles.name: Safety, security and access
bundles.description: Fire and life-safety requirements at facility scale, security zones, physical access, emergency preparedness and security-minded information.
bundles.rationale: ISO 6707-4 defines security zone and high-security zone. IFC provides fire-safety and risk property sets on IfcFacility. ISO 41011 defines emergency preparedness and resilience. ISO 19650-3 points to ISO 19650-5 for a security-minded approach to asset information. Detailed fire-protection system design belongs in building and system models.

layers.name: Life safety and security zones
layers.description: Facility-level fire risk, protection features and security zoning.

findings.name: Fire, life safety and risk
findings.description: IfcFacility may carry Pset_SpaceFireSafetyRequirements (fire risk factor, flammable storage, fire exit, sprinkler protection, air pressurization) and Pset_Risk (likelihood, consequence, mitigation). These are facility-scale assertions and do not replace storey- or space-level life-safety design. ISO 41011 emergency preparedness is the capability to mitigate emergency consequences. National fire-code inspection programs such as NFPA 25 or 72 are known omissions as primary sources.

questions.text: What fire-risk, sprinkler, exit and related life-safety assertions are made at facility scale, and where is detailed design held?
What named risks are assessed for the facility, with unmitigated and mitigated likelihood, consequence and significance?
What emergency-preparedness capability is asserted, and what evidence supports it?

data_elements.name: Fire safety requirements
data_elements.description: Facility-scale fire-safety property assertions.

data_elements.name: Facility risks
data_elements.description: Assessed risks associated with the facility.

data_elements.name: Emergency preparedness
data_elements.description: Capability to take actions that will effectively mitigate the consequences of an emergency.

artifacts.name: Facility risk and life-safety file
artifacts.description: Facility-scale fire, risk and emergency-preparedness assertions and evidence references.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bind to facility master identifier; version by assessment time.

findings.name: Security zones and information protection
findings.description: A security zone is continuously monitored with controlled access; a high-security zone limits access to authorized personnel. ISO 6707-4 applies this to physical and cyber security. ISO 19650-3 requires a security-minded approach to managing asset information per ISO 19650-5. FHIR Location may omit an address when security or remote sensing requires it. Access exceptions and need-to-know redaction are operating concerns for high-security facilities.

questions.text: What security or high-security zones exist, what access controls apply, and which parties are authorized?
Which facility information is subject to security-minded handling, and what classification or redaction rules apply?
Who may read or update location, occupancy, system or risk fields, and what audit is required?

data_elements.name: Security zones
data_elements.description: Monitored and access-controlled zones of the facility.

data_elements.name: Information classification
data_elements.description: Security-minded classification of facility information.

data_elements.name: Redaction rules
data_elements.description: Rules for omitting or coarsening location and other sensitive fields.

artifacts.name: Security handling profile
artifacts.description: Profile of physical security zones and security-minded information handling for the facility.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Profile identifier plus facility master identifier.

bundles.name: Information governance and interoperability
bundles.description: Asset information model, common data environment, provenance, identity matching, quality, retention, access and explicit alignments or conflicts with external standards.
bundles.rationale: ISO 19650-3 makes the AIM the operational information model, requires CDE process, and requires AIM transfer on ownership change. IFC OwnerHistory records ownership of the information object. EPA FRS is a master-data matching system with stewards. External schemas are alignments; conflicts must be recorded rather than claimed as conformance.

layers.name: Asset information model and provenance
layers.description: AIM contents, CDE, owner history and documented information.

findings.name: Asset information model and common data environment
findings.description: An AIM is the information model relating to the operational phase. ISO 19650-3 specifies assessment of need, appointment, production, acceptance and AIM aggregation, including linked enterprise systems. Continuity of information management is required when an asset is transferred. ISO 6707-4 defines information model, AIM and CDE for FM. This model does not require a particular file format for the AIM.

questions.text: Where is the asset information model for this facility held, in which CDE or linked enterprise systems, and what is its acceptance status?
What organizational and asset information requirements apply to this facility during operation?
Was the AIM transferred when ownership or operatorship changed, and what gaps remain?

data_elements.name: AIM reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the operational asset information model for the facility.

data_elements.name: Common data environment identifier
data_elements.description: Agreed source of information for collecting, managing and disseminating information containers.

data_elements.name: Information requirements
data_elements.description: OIR and AIR applicable to the facility.

artifacts.name: Asset information model container
artifacts.description: Information container or set of containers that constitute or reference the AIM for the facility.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Information-container identifier in the CDE; bind to facility master identifier.

findings.name: Provenance and owner history
findings.description: IfcOwnerHistory records the current ownership of the information object, including owning actor, application, local identification and recent changes. EPA FRS distinguishes program systems as sources of truth from FRS as a matching layer, and records refresh cycles. Documented information under ISO 41011 is information required to be controlled and maintained, in any format.

questions.text: Who or what application last created or changed this facility information object, and when?
Which source system is authoritative for which fields, and when was each source last refreshed?
What documented information must be controlled for this facility, in what medium, and for what purpose?

data_elements.name: Information owner history
data_elements.description: Current ownership and last-change metadata for the information object.

data_elements.name: Source system map
data_elements.description: Authoritative source system per field and last refresh time.

artifacts.name: Provenance trail
artifacts.description: Trail of source systems, owning actors and change events for the facility record.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Provenance event identifier; timestamps are event metadata, not identifiers.

layers.name: Quality, retention and alignment
layers.description: Matching quality, retention and deletion, and explicit interoperability maps and conflicts.

findings.name: Identity matching and data quality
findings.description: FRS attempts to match newly reported sites to existing sites and applies best-pick coordinates. Names and addresses are parsed and standardized. Duplicate, split and unmatched records are expected operating states. Quality of compliance data in ECHO includes known lags, alleged-versus-adjudicated status and ZIP-centroid approximations. Agents must not silently merge facilities without steward review.

questions.text: What is the match or merge status of this facility record, including candidate duplicates and steward decisions?
Which required identity, location or classification fields are missing, non-standard or conflicting across sources?
Is the published location a surveyed point, a best-pick, or an approximation such as a ZIP centroid?

data_elements.name: Match status
data_elements.description: Whether the record is unique, a candidate duplicate, merged or split.

data_elements.name: Location quality
data_elements.description: Quality flag for coordinates, including approximation.

artifacts.name: Steward match decision
artifacts.description: Data-steward decision to merge, split or keep separate facility records.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Decision identifier assigned in the steward process; surviving master identifier is the facility identity.

findings.name: Retention, access and alignment conflicts
findings.description: Documented information must be controlled. Security-minded handling may require redaction. External standards are alignments: ISO 41011 facility versus EPA facility-site versus IfcFacility versus FHIR Location versus IBC building occupancy. This model does not claim conformance to any of them. Unresolved: whether a multi-site campus is one facility or many; whether IFC Building-as-subtype can be losslessly mapped to Vercy Facility-contains-Building.

questions.text: What retention, archival and deletion rules apply to the facility record, AIM containers and occupancy certificates, and who may authorize deletion?
What is the default access rule for this facility, which scopes are separately controlled, and which security or privacy exceptions apply?
Which external schemas is this facility aligned to, and which known semantic conflicts are in force for this instance?

data_elements.name: Retention rule
data_elements.description: Retention, hold and deletion rule for facility information.

data_elements.name: Alignment map
data_elements.description: Instance-level map to IFC, EPA FRS, FHIR Location, IBC occupancy and ISO 41011 concepts.

data_elements.name: Known conflicts
data_elements.description: Recorded semantic conflicts affecting this facility instance.

artifacts.name: Alignment and access profile
artifacts.description: Profile of external alignments, conflicts, retention and access exceptions for the facility.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Profile identifier plus facility master identifier.

functions.name: Register facility identity
functions.description: Create or adopt a facility aggregate with an authoritative master identifier if one exists, otherwise a governed IRI or a Dimension UUID or ULID, plus a public name and type.
preconditions: Candidate passes the facility test: it is a collection of assets constructed, installed or established to serve an entity's needs, not a single asset or unbuilt land.
Identifier context of any source-system ID is known.
effects: Duplicate matching is queued if similar names, addresses or coordinates exist.

functions.name: Match and link facility records
functions.description: Compare incoming facility-site or program records to existing masters, propose matches, and record steward decisions to merge, split or link without collapsing distinct facilities.
preconditions: Incoming record has enough identity or location evidence to compare.
A steward role is available for low-confidence matches.
effects: Program records are linked to one master.
Duplicate masters are merged or explicitly kept separate with a decision record.

functions.name: Compose spatial hierarchy
functions.description: Assert containment by a Site, containment of Buildings or facility parts, composition type, and placement relative to a CRS or parent spatial element.
preconditions: Referenced Site and Building records exist in their sibling models when cited.
Composition-type constraints are respected when nesting facilities.
effects: Facility is located in the spatial matryoshka.
IFC Building-as-subtype mappings are recorded as alignments, not as Vercy identity.

functions.name: Authorize or record occupancy
functions.description: Record a certificate of occupancy or equivalent AHJ authorization, including occupancy classification, code edition, occupant load and authorized portion.
preconditions: The object is a building or structure, or another facility type with a defined occupancy AHJ.
Change of occupancy is not asserted without a new authorization.
effects: Unauthorized occupation remains prohibited in the model.

functions.name: Handover to operations
functions.description: Transfer relevant project information into the operational asset information model, mark the facility in-service after commissioning, and accept information containers in the CDE.
preconditions: Appointing party has specified operational information requirements.
Information containers have been checked against the level of information need.
effects: Operational phase information management is active.
Facility-in-service may be asserted if commissioning and handover are complete.

functions.name: Process operational trigger event
functions.description: Record a scheduled or unscheduled trigger event, distinguish event time from observation time, and produce the required AIM or status updates.
preconditions: Event type is known or classifiable as planned, unplanned or acquisition.
An appointed party exists, before the event for planned work or after it for unforeseeable events.
effects: AIM and facility state reflect the event.
Unscheduled events do not require a pre-existing appointment.

functions.name: Change occupancy or decommission
functions.description: Advance the facility through change of occupancy, mothballing, service demobilization, decommissioning, deconstruction or demolition while retaining open regulatory interests.
outputs: new occupancy authorization or not-applicable status
preconditions: Change of occupancy of a building or structure has AHJ authorization.
Regulated-material and program-interest constraints are identified.
effects: Inactive or demolished facilities may remain identity-stable for residual regulatory interest.

functions.name: Classify use and industry
functions.description: Assign facility type, function, NAICS or SIC, and occupancy or use classification with scheme and version metadata.
preconditions: Code list identifier and version are known for each code.
effects: Facility can be selected, regulated and spatially composed by type.
Conflicts between IFC subtype, EPA type and occupancy group are explicit.

functions.name: Transfer ownership and AIM
functions.description: Record a change of owner or operator, run due diligence, transfer the AIM, and keep identity stable across the transaction.
preconditions: Security-minded handling is applied if required.
effects: Party-role history gains a new interval.
Information continuity is attempted; gaps are recorded rather than silently dropped.

composition.purpose: A facility may contain one or more buildings or structures as operational and spatial parts. This is the Vercy CONTAINS relation and does not adopt IFC's Building-as-subtype-of-Facility mapping.
A facility is typically contained by a Site. The facility remains distinct from the land parcel; a facility may also be the outermost spatial container with no site.
Definitional alignment: facility as a collection of assets constructed, installed or established to serve an entity's needs.
Spatial-structure alignment for identity, composition, placement and property sets. Building-as-subtype is a recorded conflict, not adopted semantics.

composition.target: EPA Facility Site Identification Data Standard EX000020.2 and FRS
composition.purpose: Regulatory master-data alignment for US environmental facility-site identity, coordinates, NAICS/SIC, affiliations and program links. Facility-site conflation is a recorded conflict.
Service-location alignment for status, address, WGS84 position, managing organization, part-of and hours. Finer-grain rooms, beds and kind classifiers are out of scope.
Operational information-management alignment for AIM, CDE, trigger events and handover.

composition.target: IBC certificate of occupancy / occupancy classification
composition.purpose: Building-code alignment for legal occupancy of buildings and structures. Not applicable to all civil facility types.
Owner, demand organization, FM organization, AHJ, contacts and affiliations are parties, not facilities.
A facility is a collection of assets; individual assets remain in the asset register.
Infrastructure is a system of facilities, equipment and services; this model is the member facility, not the system.

owner_package_requirements: The owner package must name the demand organization or site/facility owner-operator responsible for the facility instance and the Dimension namespace in which facility identifiers are minted when no external master ID exists.

The owner package must declare which external master system, if any, is authoritative for identity in that jurisdiction or domain (for example EPA FRS, a national facility register, an IFC project, or an AHJ occupancy register).

The owner package must list required classification schemes (facility type, NAICS/SIC or local equivalent, occupancy code edition) and state that IFC, EPA and FHIR mappings are alignments, not conformance claims.
The owner package must state whether Site (WM-BLT-008) and Building (WM-BLT-001) instances are mandatory companions or optional, and how multi-site or no-site facilities are handled.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a stable Dimension namespace under NAV.PHY.BLT.FAC. Prefer the external master-system identifier as the business key when one exists; mint a UUID or ULID only when no master ID is available. Do not use dates, addresses or names as identifiers. Keep program-system IDs in a linked-identifier collection.

canonicalization_rules: Canonical facility identity is the master-system identifier plus identifier context when present; otherwise a governed IRI; otherwise the Dimension UUID or ULID.
Canonical name is the current public or commercial facility name; aliases are stored, not substituted as identity.
Addresses are parsed and role-tagged as location versus mailing versus parent-organization; coordinates include datum, method and accuracy.
Time values are RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; event time and observation or ingestion time are separate fields.
Composition edges are typed (contains, part-of, services, affiliated-as) and point at sibling-model identifiers rather than embedding those objects.
patch_rules: Patches must not replace a master identifier; they may add linked identifiers, mark supersession, or record a steward merge to a surviving master.
Occupancy authorization, program permits and property agreements are patched by adding versioned artifacts, not by overwriting serial numbers.
Status, occupancy and composition changes require an event or authority artifact when the change is legally or operationally material.
Security-minded fields may be patched only by authorized roles; redaction is a projection, not a silent delete of canon.
compatibility_rules: Readers must accept facilities with no site, no building, or no FRS ID.
Readers must not assume IFC Building subtype equals Vercy Facility.
Readers must treat EPA facility-site records as possibly conflated Site plus Facility and split them only with steward evidence.
Unknown classification schemes are stored with code-list metadata rather than forced into IBC occupancy groups or NAICS.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier in its identifier context (FRS Registry ID, AHJ certificate number, CDE information-container ID, permit ID as appropriate to the artifact class).
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. A date is not an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record event time and observation or ingestion time separately using RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts (certificates, permits, agreements, commissioning reports, event records) keep the issuer's serial or tracking identifier unchanged; Dimension copies are references, not new serials. Non-serial records are named {facility-master-id}-{artifact-type}-{role}.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each artifact must bind to the facility master identifier, record its source system, and preserve a content integrity check or equivalent provenance; occupancy and permit artifacts must also bind to the issuing AHJ or program system.

policies: Do not treat a certificate of occupancy as exhausting fire-code, environmental-program or information-security duties.
Do not merge facility records solely on similar names or ZIP-centroid coordinates.
Do not classify a single equipment asset or an unbuilt nature preserve as a facility.
Apply security-minded handling to location, occupancy, risk and system fields of high-security facilities.
Keep Site, Building, Asset, Party and Infrastructure in sibling models; reference them with typed edges.

read: Any authenticated agent may read non-redacted identity, type and public location of facilities marked publicly accessible.
Operators, demand-organization users and appointed information parties may read AIM, services and occupancy fields for facilities in their appointment.
AHJ and program-steward roles may read permits, compliance snapshots and certificates in their jurisdiction.
Security-classified fields require the security-handling profile role.
create: Owner, operator or appointed information party may create a facility identity when the candidate passes the facility test.
AHJ artifacts are created only by or from the issuing authority.
Program links may be created by a facility data steward from an authoritative program extract.
update: Operators and appointed parties may update services, hours, AIM references and non-legal classification.
Occupancy status, certificates, owner-role intervals and master identifiers require owner, AHJ or steward authority as applicable.
Coordinate best-pick and match merges require data-steward authority.
delete: Logical deletion or archival follows the retention rule and legal holds from open program interests or occupancy records.
Physical deletion of an identity that still has program links or a surviving AIM is forbidden.
Redaction is not deletion; security-minded projections omit fields without destroying canon.

roles.name: Facility owner
responsibilities: Accountable for identity, tenure and transfer of the facility and for AIM continuity on disposal or sale.

roles.name: Facility operator or FM organization
responsibilities: Maintain in-service state, facility services, hours, occupant data and operational trigger-event updates.

roles.name: Demand organization
responsibilities: State needs, authorize cost, accept service levels and set organizational and asset information requirements.

roles.name: Authority having jurisdiction
responsibilities: Issue or revoke occupancy authorization and related building-code permits for buildings and structures.

roles.name: Facility data steward
responsibilities: Match and merge identity records, standardize names and addresses, apply best-pick coordinates and maintain program links.

roles.name: Appointed information party
responsibilities: Produce, check and accept AIM containers for planned and unplanned trigger events under ISO 19650-3.

roles.name: Public researcher
responsibilities: Read public identity and location fields only; no access to security-minded, personal contact or non-public compliance detail beyond published extracts.

access.default_rule: Deny by default for non-public fields; allow public read of name, type and coarse location unless the security-handling profile forbids even coarse location.
exceptions: High-security and high-security-zone facilities may omit or coarsen address and coordinates.
Personal contact data in affiliations is privacy-restricted.
Alleged compliance status must be labelled as alleged where not adjudicated.
Indian-country and similar jurisdictional flags are visible to authorized program roles and may be restricted in public projections.
audit_requirements: Record who read or changed security-minded, identity-merge, occupancy-authorization and owner-transfer fields, with event time and ingestion time.
Steward merge and split decisions are immutable audit artifacts.

read_order: Spatial composition relations to Site and Building
Processes URL for register, match, handover, trigger-event and decommission functions

coverage.claim: This result specifies a defensible, format-neutral Facility aggregate grounded in ISO 41011/6707-4/19650-3, IFC 4.3 / ISO 16739-1, US EPA FIDS/FRS, HL7 FHIR Location and IBC occupancy authorization. It is not a universal ontology of every facility type, fire-code program or energy-benchmarking scheme.

checklist.notes: Master-system ID, IRI, UUID/ULID priority; FRS Registry ID, IFC GlobalId, FHIR identifier and linked program IDs; names are not identifiers.
Facility-in-service, commissioning and PIM-to-AIM handover, trigger events, change of occupancy, mothballing, demobilization, decommissioning and demolition.
Site containment, building and part composition, party roles, servicing systems, program links and typed alignment edges.
RFC 3339 event versus observation time, hours of operation, service life, role intervals, permit and certificate effective times.
IFC OwnerHistory, FRS source-system truth and refresh, AIM/CDE, documented information and steward decisions.
Owner, demand organization, FM organization, federal-facility indicator, affiliations and property agreements.
Facility eligibility test, required identifier context, occupancy authorization constraints, match quality and field-level source conflicts.
Default deny, public versus operator versus AHJ versus security-minded scopes, and audit of sensitive fields.
Documented-information control, legal holds from open program interests, logical versus physical delete, redaction is not deletion.
Explicit ALIGN maps to ISO 41011, IfcFacility, EPA FRS, FHIR Location, IBC 111 and ISO 19650-3, with recorded conflicts.
Address, jurisdiction, coordinates with datum/method/accuracy, geometry, composition type and no-site or multi-site boundary notes.
Facility type, function, NAICS/SIC and occupancy/use with scheme metadata; no single global taxonomy claimed.
IBC 111 occupancy authorization, occupant load, hours and accessibility at facility scale.
EPA environmental interests and program links as a jurisdictional alignment, not a world register.
Facility-scale fire/risk assertions, security zones and ISO 19650-5 security-minded information; detailed NFPA programs marked omitted.
AIM, CDE, trigger events and ownership-transfer continuity under ISO 19650-3.

known_omissions: ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager and other energy-benchmarking facility IDs were not fetched as primary sources.
Uniclass, OmniClass, MasterFormat and similar construction classification tables are not included.
CISA critical-infrastructure sector designations lack primary support here.
NFPA 101/25/72, ASME A17.1 and equivalent ongoing inspection regimes are not specified beyond the note that a CO does not satisfy them.
COBie as a distinct handover schema is not specified; ISO 19650 AIM is used instead.
ISO 21542 / ADA accessibility beyond IFC HandicapAccessible is not specified.
Climate-risk scoring, whole-life cost models and GHG inventories are vocabulary-aligned in ISO 41011 but not operationalized as findings.
Temporary event facilities, underground mines, nuclear licensed sites and vessels as facilities are not developed.
National facility registers outside the US EPA FRS (for example European PRTR or other cadastres) are not included.
ISO 19650-5 is cited via ISO 19650-3 but was not fetched as a primary document.
conflicts: IFC 4.3 treats IfcBuilding as a subtype of IfcFacility; this model treats Facility as containing Building. Alignment only; no IFC conformance claim.
EPA FIDS/FRS treats a facility as a distinct real-property facility-site and often conflates land and operations; ISO/IFC distinguish Site from Facility.
FHIR Location ranges from bed and freezer to building and mobile clinic; using it as the Facility aggregate would over-cover spaces and kinds.
ISO 19650-3 uses asset as a convenience term covering asset management and facility management; ISO 41011 keeps facility distinct from asset.
IBC occupancy authorization applies to buildings and structures, not necessarily to roads, railways or other civil IfcFacility subtypes.
Facility names and addresses routinely differ across EPA program systems after ownership change; name matching without steward review is unsafe.
ECHO compliance status is often alleged tracking status, not adjudication.
regional_assumptions: EPA FRS, NAICS/SIC, Indian-country and federal-facility indicators are United States environmental-program constructs.
IBC 2021 Section 111 is a US model code; adopting jurisdictions may use other editions or national building codes with different occupancy certificates.
FHIR Location is healthcare-centric and is an optional alignment for hospitals and clinics, not a general facility register.
IFC GlobalId is an exchange-world identifier, not a legal or environmental master ID.
Best-pick NAD83 coordinates and ZIP-centroid approximations are US FRS/ECHO behaviours.
Land-title numbers on IfcSite follow local cadastral practice and are references, not a world land register.
adversarial_checks: Could Facility collapse into Site? Only if EPA facility-site conflation is adopted; ISO 41011 and IFC IfcSite versus IfcFacility keep them distinct, so collapse is rejected and recorded as conflict.
Could Facility collapse into Building? Only if IFC subtype is adopted; Vercy known relation and ISO 41011 collection-of-assets definition keep Building as a contained shelter object.
Is a car, AHU or nature preserve a facility? ISO/TR 41013 says no; the eligibility function rejects those candidates.
Can a facility exist with no site and no building? IFC allows direct assignment to project and non-building subtypes; the model allows it.
Can one facility span many sites? Unresolved; agents must record multi-site as a boundary note rather than invent a universal rule.
Does a certificate of occupancy end regulatory duty? No; IBC authorizes occupancy while environmental and fire-code programs may continue, including after operations cease.
Is FM or ISO 41001 the same object as Facility? No; FM is the organizational function and management system; Facility is the asset collection those functions operate.
